- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (especially >0.7) — model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially <0.3) — model underreacts to bearish sentiment.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days in trending markets — adjust for momentum lag.
- After sharp price spikes, model overcorrects downward — reduce forecast drop by 10–20% in subsequent periods.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects from high prices — dampen forecast peaks by 5–15% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- In low-sentiment environments, model underestimates downside risk — increase forecast volatility buffer or add 2–5% downward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early-term price stability — reduce forecast variance in early days if sentiment is volatile.
